title: Road trip planning with Sam
description: Demo conversation (synthetic, for the demo account). Alex and Sam plan their summer coast road trip, covering route, budget and where to sleep; Sam's camping gear question is deferred and picked up at the end, while a story about Sam's cousin's wedding is never told.

utterances.text: Okay, I brought snacks and a map. An actual paper map.
Who even sells those anymore? Okay, coast road trip. Last week of July, like we said.
Yes. So, route. I'm thinking we start in the north and drive south, so the ocean is on your side the whole way.
Wait, really? That matters?
For the views, totally. Plus the pull-outs are easier to get into from that lane.
Okay, north to south. How many days?
Six, I think. Five if we skip the lighthouse town, but we're not skipping the lighthouse town.
Obviously. I want at least one day where we don't drive more than two hours. Just beach and a book.
Done. Day four, beach day. Okay, money. What are you thinking?
Honestly, I might be changing jobs, so I want to keep it cheap. Like six hundred each, max?
That's doable. Gas split two ways is maybe a hundred and fifty each. Food if we cook most nights, another two hundred.
So sleeping is the expensive part.
Right. Which is why I think we camp most nights. Oh, and we need to figure out camping gear, but let's sort that out later.
Okay, later. So campgrounds, but I want one real bed. One motel night, with a shower that isn't a coin box.
Fair. Middle of the trip? Night three?
Night three. And maybe we book the campgrounds now? The good ones by the water fill up by June.
Yeah, I'll book tonight. Oh, remind me to tell you about my cousin's wedding, it's chaos.
Ha, okay. Can we also make a rule about music? Each person gets the aux for one hour, no complaining.
Even if you play the same album four times?
Especially then. That's the deal.
Fine. And no phones at dinner. We're going to the ocean, not to scroll.
Agreed. Okay, what else is left?
Oh, right. Camping gear. So I have a tent, but it's a two-person tent, which means a one-and-a-half-person tent.
I can borrow my brother's bigger one. And I have the little stove and the cooler.
Perfect. Then I'll bring sleeping pads and the lantern. Do you have a sleeping bag?
An old one. It smells like a basement, but it's warm.
We'll air it out on day one. Okay, I think that's a whole trip.
Coast, six days, six hundred bucks, one motel. I'm so ready.
